llm_reasoning: Fluid Intelligence (Gf) is a domain-general cognitive ability encompassing novel problem-solving, abstract reasoning, working memory, and cognitive flexibility. Meta-analyses (Neurosynth, BrainMap) and individual fMRI studies consistently implicate the following networks: (1) The Frontoparietal Network (FPN) is the core hub: dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (Frontal_Sup, Frontal_Mid) and posterior parietal cortex (Parietal_Sup, Parietal_Inf, Angular, SupraMarginal) show the most reliable activation across matrix reasoning, Raven's, and abstract pattern tasks. (2) The Anterior Cingulate / Cognitive Control system (Cingulum_Ant, Frontal_Sup_Medial) supports conflict monitoring and executive control. (3) The Salience Network (Insula) facilitates network switching. (4) The Cerebellar-Cortical loops, particularly lateral lobules 6, 7b, 8, 9, 10 and Crus I/II, contribute to working memory, rule abstraction, and cognitive timing. (5) Subcortical relays: Caudate (cognitive/working memory), Thalamus (MD nucleus relay to PFC), and to a lesser extent Putamen. (6) The Default Mode Network (Precuneus, Cingulum_Post, medial PFC) is reliably deactivated during Gf tasks, indicating its involvement in the network dynamics. (7) Temporal regions (especially superior temporal) show modest involvement in verbal-analytic components. Primary sensory/motor cortices, olfactory cortex, and vermis show negligible Gf-specific involvement. Lateralization is minimal for Gf; both hemispheres contribute roughly equally to the FPN, though slight left-hemisphere advantage in verbal-analytic subcomponents is noted.
